known_bad.decision: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-26 08:27. The gate now PASSES on this candidate: `0 net(s) with no global route; 0 open net(s) declined`. known_bad.what: Every published stream in this project carries an Artifactory property named `layout.canonical_hash`, written by scripts/ci/gds_canonical_hash.py. The name reads like a layout identity and the value cannot support that reading. MEASURED 2026-08-26 on this candidate and its reference: KLayout strmxor 0.30.10 reports NO DIFFERENCES between _DRYRUN_20260826_rc1v3r4 and _DRYRUN_20260826_v3r4 across all 49 layer/datatype pairs, while the two canonical hashes are DIFFERENT (48891f86d4865fab0d607a56... vs 3f90ad3babba0298ca521098...) at identical byte count (302,688,050) and identical record count (34,791,830). The cause is known and is not in the tool: write_stream is not order-deterministic. Re-streaming one database on 26 Aug produced 26,842 differing bytes, 12,600 of them BGNLIB/BGNSTR clocks and 14,242 decoding as padring filler SREFs (PFILLER5_G, PFILLER20_G, PCORNER_G) emitted in another order in the top cell.
known_bad.decision: NOT withdrawn and NOT rewritten. The digest is CORRECT for what it computes and the raw md5/sha256 beside it are load-bearing -- a foundry Final Report cites the md5. What is wrong is the DIRECTION anyone may read into it, so the direction is now carried with the number instead of being left to the reader: gds_canonical_hash.py returns a `claim` field saying a MATCH implies the same layout and a MISMATCH implies nothing, and its --selftest gained an arm that proves the order sensitivity in a fixture (two files holding the same two rectangles in opposite record order: identical byte and record counts, different digest). The layout question is now answered properly and separately, by a geometric arbiter: scripts/ci/gds_xor_arbiter.py, wired in as the `gds-layout-identity` gate and proved both directions in its own selftest. An order-insensitive element-multiset digest IS the right cheap streaming answer if one is ever wanted -- it was run ad hoc on 26 Aug and returned IDENTICAL for 2,267 structures and 6,210,067 elements -- but it is a second approximation of a question the arbiter now answers exactly, so none was implemented. THE PUBLISH PATH WAS NOT TOUCHED: renaming a live store property is a store change, it would orphan the key on already-published artifacts, and a republish is being co-ordinated separately.
known_bad.withdraw_when: the store stops publishing this digest under a `layout.*` name -- either renamed to something that says RECORD SEQUENCE, or accompanied by the gds-layout-identity gate's verdict as a sibling property so a consumer reading the store sees the geometric answer next to the record one. Until then, treat a `layout.canonical_hash` mismatch as a prompt to run the arbiter and never as a finding.

xor_reference.why: CHOSEN, not defaulted, and the choice is the claim. The two available references answer different questions. (a) A RE-STREAM of this run's own ECO'd database would prove only that write_stream renders that database faithfully -- a self-consistency check that can catch a writer bug and nothing else, and it needs an Innovus session on a read-only tree. (b) _DRYRUN_20260826_v3r4 (md5 70858177e4b9cca11daf201f52eeb45d) is the SAME INTENDED LAYOUT REACHED BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE: it descends from gdsrun-20260825-resynth via a hand ECO on the pgeco database, while this candidate is a full flow from RTL a day later with the same edits landed in-flow through hooks/post_powerplan.tcl plus one marker-driven post-route ECO. A zero XOR between them is therefore a REPRODUCIBILITY result, and it is the stronger of the two: it says two independent syntheses, placements, CTSs and routes converge on the same polygons, and it carries every geometric measurement made on _v3r4 -- its Calibre four-tier 737/46/13/0 and its LVS -- across to these bytes unchanged. WHAT A ZERO DOES NOT PROVE, either way: that either stream is CORRECT (DRC, LVS and LEC answer that, and lec-rtl-to-gate is still NOT-MEASURED here), and nothing about the foundry's merged view, which adds dummy fill and a seal ring that are not in these bytes.
